beats.t: The courtroom was a giant birdcage. Curved iron bars rose into the sky. On every tier inside sat silent people bearing gray stamps.
Yeoni hung in the defendant's place, still in the net. It had not loosened at all through the night.
Do defendants have human rights here? Or at least pig rights?
The robed crow landed on the high dais. Its eyes remained hidden behind the mask. A feather gavel tapped the table once.
Court is in session.
Defendant: Flower Pig. Three charges. Incitement to song, unauthorized fine dining, excessive exclamations.
That third one's a crime I've genuinely never heard of.
Records show the defendant uttered forty-seven exclamations yesterday.
You were counting those?
Forty-eight.
Examples will be read aloud. Oink. Oiiink. Oink-aaah. Wow. Awesome. Insane.
Hearing them in the judge's voice is really embarrassing.
Oink-aaah is a word I haven't heard either.
You heard it too! On the first day!
A few shoulders on the tiers trembled with suppressed laughter. The crow's head whipped toward them. The shoulders froze.
Where is the defense counsel's place?
Yeongnyangi was bound beside the witness stand, tightly wrapped in feathers. His voice, at least, carried clearly through the court.
The defendant has not been granted counsel.
Under this island's law, a performer may have one applauder. I will fill that role.
There was a law like that?
Just thought of it.
Best lawyer. Five stars.
...Granted. On condition that the applauder does not applaud.
Clapping with cat paws is difficult anyway.
Exhibit One.
A crow brought a silver tray. On it lay a half-eaten rice-cake skewer. Yeoni's eyes lit up.
Oh, my skewer.
Yeoni. Drooling over the evidence makes defending you difficult.
It's not my fault my body reacts first.
Flavor was detected in this skewer. State its source.
Yeoni pressed their mouth shut. Moka's name rose to their tongue, then retreated.
Found it on the ground. Anyway, I found it.
False testimony added.
Objection. The person eating cannot be held responsible for the food being delicious.
Overruled.
Objection. An exclamation cannot automatically be classified as a song.
The defendant's oiiink had pitch. Falling from sol to mi.
You assigned solfège to my scream?
...Now that you mention it, it was sol to mi.
Yeongnyangi! Whose side are you on!
Your Honor, I challenge the storage conditions of the evidence. The skewer has gone cold.
Why is that a problem?
A cold skewer has no flavor. Without flavor, unauthorized fine dining cannot be established.
Oh, that sounded kind of lawyerly.
Overruled. The defendant drooled even at the cold skewer.
Call the witness.
The barred door opened. The old woman from the gray market entered, three stamps on her hand. Seeing Yeoni, she bowed her head a little.
Witness. Did this pig sing in the market?
The woman could not answer. The stamps had taken even her speech. Instead, she brought her hands together before her chest, then slowly opened them.
What does that mean?
A flower blooming. When you ate her candy and smiled at the market.
She nodded once. A few people on the tiers opened their hands too. Silent flowers bloomed throughout the courtroom.
Enough.
For the first time, the crow's voice cracked. The people hurriedly lowered their hands.
Um, Your Honor. Can I ask one thing?
The defendant may not ask questions.
Then I'll talk to myself. Why would someone hate singing this much? Did a song slap the judge in the face?
I've been laughed at plenty for singing badly too. My highest karaoke score was forty-seven.
Forty-seven. The same as today's exclamation count.
The courtroom went still. The claws gripping the feather gavel whitened.
Singing invites ridicule.
If nobody sings, nobody laughs at anyone.
...Who laughed at you?
The gavel slammed the table. It cracked. The crows on the bars spread their wings in unison.
Verdict.
Defendant Flower Pig: entire voice confiscated. Applauder Cat: hat confiscated for complicity.
His hat? Why Yeongnyangi's hat!
The loudest hat in the world.
I'll take that as a compliment.
Two crows approached Yeongnyangi with scissors. The blades touched the tassel at the hat's tip. One golden strand fell to the floor.
Yeongnyangi did not blink. Yeoni's breathing quickened instead. Their heartbeat drummed in their ears.
Don't touch him.
The defendant may not speak.
I said, don't touch him!
The words leaving Yeoni's mouth became fire. Letter-shaped flames leaped into the air. DON'T. TOUCH. HIM. NOW. Four masses of flame melted the scissors.
...Hurting Officer.
The fire did not stop. With every breath Yeoni took, the words grew hotter. The iron bars glowed red. People on the tiers edged away.
If you hate singing, just don't sing yourself! Why shut everyone else's mouths!
Yeoni, stop!
You like everyone living in silence? You like an island with nothing to laugh about that much?
One flame curved toward the tiers, toward the old woman's seat. Yeongnyangi tore through the feathers binding him and leaped.
White light collided with red fire. Yeongnyangi's paw knocked the flame aside. It skimmed over the woman's head, struck the bars, and scattered.
Y-Yeongnyangi?
I'm fine. Breathe first. Slowly.
Yeoni drew breath. The fire dwindled. A burned smell remained in their mouth. Yeongnyangi was hiding a paw behind his back.
I nearly hit her.
If you had, I would have scolded you. You didn't. That's enough.
Did you see? Words are fire. That is why they must be stopped.
At that moment, metal clattered in the roof vent. Rattle. Rattle. Something was rolling down.
Your fried food is ready!
Moka dropped from the vent and overturned a pot of oil. As lumps of batter touched the heat from the bars, white smoke erupted.
Clear the smoke!
Too late. Grandma's smokescreen fritters last ten minutes.
You can make a smokescreen out of fried food?
Double the flour in the batter. Tastes awful, though. Don't eat it.
That's the saddest part.
Moka's kitchen knife cut the net's edge. Yeoni tumbled from the defendant's stand. Yeongnyangi caught their scruff in his mouth and hauled them up.
The exit?
Sewer. Put up with the smell if you want to live.
These net marks already make me a patterned pig, and now a sewer too?
Mourn your pattern later. Run.
The sewer emerged below a seaside hill. The evening sea was silent. Waves broke without a splash.
Looks like the sea got stamped too.
Since the day the sun stopped. The waves shut their mouths.
Moka retrieved the small ember jar from behind a rock. He fried flat pancakes from the remaining batter. This time they smelled right.
Eat. These are the tasty ones.
One bite spread the rich flavor of oil. Yeoni's ears fluttered on their own.
Thanks. ...But why did you come? If they catch you, you get stamped too.
I told you, hearing it makes you an accomplice. What kind of accomplice abandons another accomplice?
You're surprisingly loyal.
Not surprisingly. Openly.
Halfway through the pancake, Yeoni stopped. Their hoof tips still stung where the fire had passed.
That was me earlier. My words turned into fire.
Hurting Officer. The sharpest of the forces flowing from within you to the outside.
Then what about Eating God?
The same fire, burning in a way that lets someone eat and smile.
Put simply, fire for grilling skewers versus fire that burns a house. Same fire, different use.
Oh. Teacher Moka explains it better.
I'm a cat. Not good at metaphors. Hmph.
Grandma said songs were what raised the sun. If everyone sang at noon, it climbed to its highest point.
Then singing at noon will make the sun move again?
An old story. A fairy tale. Don't actually believe it.
I'm very good at believing fairy tales.
Byeong is the midday sun. If this sun cannot pass noon, that story is not wrong.
...Really? Then Grandma was right?
The laughter settled. Yeoni hugged their knees and watched the silent waves.
That crow, when its voice cracked earlier... It looked like it really hurt.
Don't pity it. That thing tore down my grandmother's shop sign.
It's not pity. I just wonder who laughed.
Nobody answered. Soon, Yeoni's breathing slowed. The pig fell asleep with pancake still in their mouth.
Yeongnyangi walked alone to the water and dipped his forepaw into the silent waves.
Steam rose. Beneath the white fur, the skin was blackened. The burn resembled a character. 傷—wound.
...Faster than I expected.
Yeongnyangi withdrew the paw and brushed fur over it. When he looked back, Yeoni was still asleep.
At the same time, in the empty courtroom, the crow picked up the golden tassel strand from the floor.
Hurting Officer has awakened. At this rate, noon will come.
The crow tucked the strand inside its robes. A black feather trembled there all by itself. There was no wind.
Before then, I will devour that pig's voice.
